title: How big is the UK gym membership market each year? About £4.28B a year, estimated step by step
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How big is the UK gym membership market each year?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: Here is a step up to practise on. Read the question, pause, and have a go at your own estimate first, even a rough one. Then walk through the answer below and compare. Your number does not need to match; your logic is what counts.
body:
The question

How big is the UK gym membership market each year?

The approach

People × share with a membership × monthly fee × 12.

Say this out loud before you touch any numbers. It lets the interviewer agree with your plan, or nudge you, before you have done any work.

Step by step

  1. People in the UK: 68M
  2. × 15% have a gym membership
  3. × £35 average monthly fee
  4. × 12 months

That gives about £4.28B a year.

Does it make sense?

About 10 million members at budget-to-mid prices; budget chains pull the average fee down.

This sanity check is the step most people skip, and one of the easiest ways to impress. It shows you care whether the number is right, not just whether the sum works.

Real-world check

Industry reports for 2025 to 2026 put UK gym membership at about 12 million people (around 18% of the population) and the market at roughly £6.5 to £7.3 billion. The estimate lands lower mainly because premium clubs pull the real average fee up. That is the value of a sanity check: it shows which assumption to revisit.

Source: Health Club Management: UK fitness market data.

Your turn

outro: If your estimate was far off, look for which step made the difference. That is where the learning is, and it is exactly what an interviewer would ask about.
